newsitem.title: FRANCE: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE IN NEW CONTROVERSY.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE IN NEW CONTROVERSY.

text.p: Canadian Jacques Villeneuve was involved in a new Formula One controversy on Friday as world championship leader Michael Schumacher topped the times in rain-hit practice for Sunday's French Grand Prix.

Villeneuve, 28, wound up fifth-fastest for Williams after causing a stir in the paddock with comments suggesting that Formula One was too politically correct -- and that the drivers were insincere in their expressed feelings for injured rival Olivier Panis.

Villeneuve, who was reprimanded by the sports ruling body the International Motoring Federation (FIA) two weeks ago for his colourful and outspoken criticism of the 1998 rule changes, also said he felt that Panis's injuries -- two broken legs -- were not something to cause serious concern.
"As a driver you know the risk is there every time you go out," said Villeneuve. "I am not saying it should be more dangerous, but when you think about it two broken legs is not that bad.
"That happens to everyone at some point in their life."
Frenchman Panis suffered double fractures to both of his legs when he crashed his Prost car during the Canadian Grand Prix.
Villeneuve's comments provoked strong reactions, but few of his fellow drivers were prepared to become involved in a war of words.
Schumacher, however, said: "I was genuinely concerned when I saw Olivier. You are not human if that sort of incident does not effect you."

In the rain-hit practice, Germany's double world champion was quickest in his Ferrari ahead of Italian Giancarlo Fisichella in a Jordan, Mika Hakkinen of Finland in a McLaren and Ralf Schumacher in the second Jordan.
Villeneuve was fifth with his Williams team-mate Heinz-Harald Frentzen sixth.
World champion Damon Hill of Britain, who was second fastest during the rain in the first hour, finished up 13th in his Arrows.
